question: With the same tools, can a task-anonymous scheduler use matched feedback to choose when blending or retaining a single model is worthwhile?
control: The already registered expanded cold-start arm, with identical four new heads and underlying library. No feature or candidate hint, no supervised warm start, identical raw package, folds, 20-fit limit and offline execution.
intervention: The public solve entry receives only the general matched-finalists planning mode. After at least three actual results, the planner measures equal votes from paired predictions. It can extend its two strongest improving pairs with a third candidate. A blend may enter a race only if it beats the leading single and each proper component subset on the primary fold. Without such a blend, a close, error-complementary single can challenge. When checking is affordable and delaying would consume the remaining opportunities, lock the participants and still-untouched, disjoint confirmation folds. Reserve every missing measurement and all possible refits. If no evidence supports a race, keep the original scheduling policy.
selection: Rank singles on matched training folds, protecting the initial leader from challengers that lose on average on fresh groups. Deploy a vote only for at least 0.003 pooled improvement over the comparison singles and proper subsets, positive fresh-group average versus every comparator, and no fresh fold losing to the selected single. The original single, a different single, a two-model vote or a three-model vote can win. Log the lock before seeing these labels as outcomes and retain every comparison.
external: Seal all three autonomous prediction files before scoring the 940 development validation rows once. The previously reported historical score on these rows is known. No course test or H2 input.
